description:
## Why
```
defmodule Names do
  @spec name(atom()) :: String.t()
  def name(module), do: Atom.to_string(module)
end
IO.inspect(Names.name(Foo.Bar))
```
stops the compiler with four internal/unresolved-wait errors (a call's return type, a function's contract, entry dispatch, input demand; all at <generated>). With binary() in place of String.t() it prints "Elixir.Foo.Bar", as Elixir does. Found in fixture 00699's oracle twin.

## What changes
A remote type String.t() in a @spec resolves, and the program prints "Elixir.Foo.Bar" on run, interp and build.

## Signal
A new fixture with the program above passes on all three paths; no internal/unresolved-wait.
title: A @spec whose return is String.t() compiles
